title: Expo TypeScript scaffold that lints, typechecks and builds
description: Create the Expo (React Native) application in TypeScript and nothing else. No test framework, and none of the app's feature dependencies — those are TASK-013 and TASK-014. This task exists only to prove the toolchain works, because everything after it fails confusingly if it does not. An earlier version of this task also installed seven dependencies and configured Jest, and exhausted a 100-turn budget twice without committing anything; the work was not wrong, there was simply too much of it for one run.
acceptanceCriteria: The repository holds an Expo application in TypeScript that renders one placeholder screen
`tsconfig.json` sets `strict: true`, and `npm run typecheck` reports no errors
`npm run lint` and `npm run build` each exit 0, and `build` needs no Xcode, Android Studio or native toolchain
`npm test` exists and exits 0 — a placeholder is correct here, because TASK-013 installs the test framework and CI must stay green in between
A lockfile is committed, and `npm ci` installs from it without modifying it
No dependency beyond what the Expo TypeScript template itself requires is installed

title: Jest and React Native Testing Library, with one passing test
description: Install and configure the test framework so every later task can write tests. This is its own task because the React Native Jest preset and its transform configuration are the fiddliest part of the setup, and a run that has to get them right alongside everything else gets neither.
acceptanceCriteria: Jest and `@testing-library/react-native` are installed, and `npm test` runs Jest rather than a placeholder
One test renders the placeholder screen and asserts it renders without throwing
Tests run with no device, simulator or emulator available, as they must in CI
`npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` each exit 0
The committed lockfile is updated, and `npm ci` installs from it without modifying it

title: Install the four feature dependencies the app will need
description: Install the runtime dependencies later tasks require, and prove each one loads. Installing them together, once, keeps a single task responsible for package.json — no later task may change dependencies, so anything missing here is a specification error to report rather than to install.
acceptanceCriteria: `react-native-svg`, `react-native-reanimated`, `expo-notifications` and `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage` are all installed at versions Expo supports for this SDK
`react-native-reanimated` is wired into the Babel configuration as its documentation requires, since it does not work without that
A test imports each of the four and asserts the import succeeds, so a broken install fails here rather than three tasks later
`npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` each exit 0
The committed lockfile is updated, and `npm ci` installs from it without modifying it

title: The hydration domain model, as pure functions
description: Implement the rules of the app as pure TypeScript with no React, no storage and no platform imports: a daily goal, a day's logged entries, and the arithmetic over them. Every later task reads its behaviour from here rather than reimplementing it, so this is where correctness is decided and where it is cheapest to test.
acceptanceCriteria: A goal is an amount in millilitres; creating one with zero, a negative number, a non-integer or a non-number throws a TypeError rather than returning an invalid goal
Adding an entry returns a new day value and never mutates the day it was given
`progress` returns a number from 0 to 1, clamped at 1 when the goal is exceeded, and 0 for a day with no entries
Goal met is true when the total is greater than or equal to the goal, and remains true if the goal is later raised above the total only when the total still meets it
Undoing removes the single most recent entry, and is a no-op that throws nothing on a day with no entries
Each entry carries an ISO 8601 timestamp, and the time since the last entry is `null` for a day with no entries rather than zero or infinity
No file in this task imports React, React Native, or any storage or platform module
`npm test` covers each criterion above, and lint, typecheck and build exit 0

title: On-device persistence behind a swappable interface
description: Persist the goal, today's entries and previous days' totals to the device using AsyncStorage, reached through an interface so tests can substitute an in-memory implementation. Nothing leaves the device, there is no account, and there is no network call anywhere in this task.
acceptanceCriteria: The goal and the current day's entries survive closing and reopening the app
Each past day is retained under its own date key, so history is not overwritten when a new day starts
Stored data that is absent, empty, or not valid JSON yields documented defaults instead of throwing
Storage is defined as an interface with an AsyncStorage implementation and an in-memory implementation, and every test in this task uses the in-memory one
No test in this task calls AsyncStorage directly
`npm test` covers each criterion above, and lint, typecheck and build exit 0

title: Set and change the daily goal
description: A screen where the user sets their daily water goal in millilitres and changes it at any point during the day. Changing the goal must not disturb what has already been logged — the two are independent, and conflating them is the obvious way to get this wrong.
acceptanceCriteria: The goal can be set, is persisted, and is shown as the current value when the app is reopened
The goal can be changed while entries already exist that day, and the logged entries are unchanged by it
Zero, negative, non-numeric and empty input are rejected with a message visible on screen, and nothing is written to storage
The screen reads and writes through the storage interface from TASK-003 rather than touching AsyncStorage itself
`npm test` covers each criterion above, and lint, typecheck and build exit 0

title: Log a glass, undo it, and see where the day stands
description: The main screen: tap to log a glass, see today's total and what remains, and undo a mistake. This is the screen the user opens ten times a day, so it must be one tap to log and must persist immediately rather than on some later event.
acceptanceCriteria: Logging a glass of a chosen size increases today's total and is persisted before the interaction completes
Undo removes the most recent glass and restores the previous total
Today's total, the goal, and the amount remaining are all visible without scrolling
When the date changes, a new day starts at zero and the previous day's total is retained in history rather than discarded
Reopening the app on the same day shows the same total, not a reset one
`npm test` covers each criterion above, including the date change, and lint, typecheck and build exit 0

title: The blob character, as a presentational component
description: An SVG blob character whose appearance is a function of two props and nothing else: how far through the goal the day is, and what mood it should show. It holds no state, reads no storage, and knows nothing about water — which is what makes it testable and what stops it becoming the place where logic accidentally lives.
acceptanceCriteria: The component takes a `progress` prop between 0 and 1 and a `mood` prop, and takes no other input
Its rendered size is a pure function of `progress`, asserted at 0, 0.5 and 1 with three different results
At a progress of 1 or above it renders its happy variant, and below 1 it does not
Rendering twice with identical props produces identical output — no randomness, no time-dependence
No file in this task imports from the storage or domain modules
`npm test` covers each criterion above, and lint, typecheck and build exit 0

title: Animate the blob's growth and celebration
description: Give the blob smooth motion using Reanimated: it grows towards its new size when a glass is logged rather than snapping, and celebrates when the goal is reached. Because no automated check can judge whether motion looks good, the criteria below constrain what is verifiable — the timings, the triggers, and the accessibility escape hatch — and leave the aesthetics to be tuned by hand afterwards.
acceptanceCriteria: The blob's size transitions between progress values over time using Reanimated rather than changing in a single frame
Logging a glass triggers the growth transition, and reaching the goal triggers a distinct celebration animation that the growth transition alone does not produce
Animation durations are exported named constants, and tests assert the triggers use them rather than inline numbers
When the operating system's reduce-motion setting is enabled, animations are skipped and the blob renders directly at its final size
No animation blocks logging a glass: a second glass can be logged while an animation is still running
`npm test` covers each criterion above, and lint, typecheck and build exit 0

title: Local reminders when the user has not had a drink for a while
description: Schedule local notifications with expo-notifications when no glass has been logged for a configured interval. These are scheduled on the device — there is no server, no push service, and no credential of any kind. Scheduling goes through an interface so tests can assert what would have been scheduled without scheduling anything.
acceptanceCriteria: When the configured interval passes with no glass logged, a local notification is scheduled reminding the user to drink
Logging a glass cancels any pending reminder and schedules the next one from that moment
Once the day's goal is met, no further reminders are scheduled for that day
If the user denies notification permission, the app continues to work with no crash, and the denial is recorded so the user is not asked repeatedly
Scheduling is defined as an interface with a real implementation and a fake, and no test schedules a real notification or requests a real permission
No code in this task performs a network request
`npm test` covers each criterion above, and lint, typecheck and build exit 0

title: Settings: reminder interval, quiet hours, and an off switch
description: A settings screen controlling the reminder behaviour built in TASK-008. Quiet hours matter more than they look: a hydration app that wakes someone at three in the morning gets deleted, so the window must be respected at scheduling time rather than by dismissing notifications after they fire.
acceptanceCriteria: The reminder interval is configurable, persists, and changing it reschedules any pending reminder
Quiet hours are configurable as a start and end time, and no reminder is scheduled to fire inside that window
A quiet-hours window that crosses midnight is handled correctly rather than treated as an empty range
Notifications can be switched off entirely, which cancels everything already scheduled
All settings persist through the storage interface and survive reopening the app
`npm test` covers each criterion above, including the window crossing midnight, and lint, typecheck and build exit 0

title: Recent history and the current streak
description: Show the last seven days and the current streak of days on which the goal was met. Each day is judged against the goal that applied on that day, not today's goal, so raising the goal does not retroactively break a past success.
acceptanceCriteria: The last seven days are listed, each showing that day's total against the goal that applied on that day
The current streak counts consecutive days on which the goal was met, ending today or yesterday
A day with no recorded data counts as not met and breaks the streak rather than being skipped
A streak of zero renders without error, as does a history containing no days at all
Today counts towards the streak only once its goal has actually been met
`npm test` covers each criterion above, and lint, typecheck and build exit 0

title: First-run onboarding
description: On first launch, walk the user through setting an initial goal and asking for notification permission, then never show it again. Skipping must leave a working app rather than a broken one — an onboarding flow that can strand the user is worse than no onboarding at all.
acceptanceCriteria: On first launch the app shows onboarding that sets an initial daily goal and requests notification permission
Completing onboarding is recorded, and it does not appear on any subsequent launch
Skipping onboarding leaves a usable app with a documented default goal and reminders switched off
Onboarding does not appear again after the app is reopened, whether it was completed or skipped
`npm test` covers each criterion above, and lint, typecheck and build exit 0

title: A README that explains how to run and use the app
description: Document the finished app for someone who has never seen it: what it does, how to run it on a phone with Expo Go, how to run the checks, and how the reminders actually behave. This task exists because a finished app nobody can start is not finished, and because the reminder rules are the part a user will otherwise have to read the source to understand.
acceptanceCriteria: `README.md` explains what the app does in a short opening paragraph
It gives the exact commands to install dependencies and start the app, and to open it on a phone using Expo Go
It lists the commands for lint, typecheck, test and build, and every command it lists runs successfully against the repository as it stands
It describes when reminders fire, how quiet hours affect them, and how to switch them off
It states that data is stored only on the device, with no account and no server, and that clearing app data loses history
It documents that animations are skipped when the operating system's reduce-motion setting is on
Lint, typecheck, test and build all exit 0
